item.title: Kanzi the bonobo could play pretend — a trait thought unique to humans
item.description: Past anecdotal observations have hinted that great apes play pretend. But now, experimental research shows that our closest living relatives can keep track of imaginary objects.

item.title: Spotted lanternflies are invading the US. They may have gotten their evolutionary superpowers in China's cities.
item.description: The alarming spread of spotted lanternflies across the U.S. has been made possible by cities acting as evolutionary incubators, fine-tuning the insects and enabling them to thrive.

item.title: The 'mono' virus raises the risk of MS and cancer in some. 22 genes hint at why.
item.description: An infection with Epstein-Barr virus is a nonevent for most people. But for a subset, the virus can contribute to chronic conditions and cancer, and genes may play a role in that risk.

item.title: Every major galaxy is speeding away from the Milky Way, except one — and we finally know why
item.description: A vast, flat sheet of dark matter may solve the long-standing mystery of why our neighboring galaxy Andromeda is speeding toward us while our other neighbors are moving away from us.

item.title: Bandera Volcano Ice Cave: The weird lava tube in New Mexico whose temperature is always below freezing
item.description: Due to a weird quirk of geology, New Mexico's Bandera Volcano Ice Cave never warms above 31 degrees Fahrenheit, even when temperatures outside exceed 100 F in summer.

item.title: Psychedelic drug ayahuasca could treat PTSD, early studies hint. But exactly how it works isn't clear.
item.description: Using methods such as brain scans and symptom tracking, scientists are beginning to study whether a complex psychedelic brew known as ayahuasca can help rewire the brain's response to trauma.

item.title: Psychedelics may rewire the brain to treat PTSD. Scientists are finally beginning to understand how.
item.description: New research shows MDMA and psilocybin may restore neural flexibility in people with PTSD, thereby helping the brain unlearn fear and relearn safety.

item.title: Scientist accidentally stumbles across bizarre ancient ‘wrinkle structures’ in Morocco that shouldn't be there
item.description: Ancient fossil structures imprinted on rocks that were once deep beneath the ocean suggest the search for the first life on Earth needs to be broadened.

item.title: Extraordinary photo captures first appearance of Siberian peregrine falcon in Australia's arid center
item.description: An ecologist has captured a photo of a peregrine falcon subspecies in an unprecedented location.

item.title: 'Invisible scaffolding of the universe' revealed in ambitious new James Webb telescope images
item.description: A team of researchers using the James Webb Space Telescope has produced the most detailed map of dark matter to date.
